subject: RFI: Flex commit safeguard, price indexation and overage mechanics
messages:
From: John Davila <john.davila@hearthbank.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: RFI: price indexation and commit protection questions

Marcus —

Thanks for taking the time on this RFI. We have a couple of focused commercial questions so we can compare apples-to-apples across vendors. Attached is our 12–24 month usage forecast. Please confirm the semantics and any limitations for the items below: 

1) Price indexation: can Redwood index list/commit prices to a published inflation metric (US CPI-U)? If yes, what default cap/floor do you apply (absolute % or band)? Is there an alternative fixed escalator you offer for multiyear deals?

2) Currency and FX: our agreement will be priced in USD but invoiced locally; do you offer FX protection (fixed USD invoicing with quarterly translation) or a pass-through approach? How are overages handled across currency fluctuation?

3) Commit smoothing / grace banding: can committed token volume be smoothed across quarters with a rolling grace band before overage rates apply? If so, what lookback/true-up cadence do you recommend?

4) Overage mechanics & tiered discounts: do overage rates default to a fixed surcharge over the commit unit price (e.g., 1.25x) or do you use banded overage tiers with marginal pricing? Can we define a volume-discount ladder that triggers at 1.25x and 1.5x commit usage?

5) Credits on termination / early exits: any standard crediting for prepaid commits if we scale down early?

If you can provide a short worked example (three-year commit, annual true-ups, CPI cap options) that would be ideal.

Thanks — appreciate concise bullets.

John

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>

John —

Thanks for the clear list and the forecast — useful. Below are concise, production-focused answers and one recommended commercial template we use for multiyear enterprise deals. If you want, we can walk through the worked example on a short call.

1) Price indexation
- Option A (indexation): Redwood supports indexing to US CPI-U (published monthly). Standard commercial guard rails: annual adjustment applied on the contract anniversary, capped at +3.0% and floored at 0% (i.e., no negative downward adjustments). This protects both parties from runaway inflation while keeping unit economics predictable.
- Option B (fixed escalator): 0% / 2.0% / 2.5% fixed annual step (customer choice at signing).

2) Currency and FX
- Default: list and commits denominated in USD; invoices can be issued in local currency at our published monthly FX rate. For customers who require FX certainty, we offer fixed-USD invoicing (no translation) with a small administrative FX fee (0.5% of invoice) and quarterly reconciliation. Overage invoices follow the same currency election for the billing period.

3) Commit smoothing / grace banding
- We support a rolling quarterly smoothing window with a 15% per-quarter grace band before overages apply. Quarterly true-ups (invoice offset model): usage above the annualized committed run rate is invoiced at overage tiers; under-usage is carried forward to the next quarter up to a 12-month lookback. This model reduces spike sensitivity while keeping billing transparent.

4) Overage mechanics & tiered discounts
- Recommended default: marginal overage tiers — first 10% above commit priced at 1.25x commit unit price, next 25% at 1.15x, and all incremental at 1.0x (i.e., converts to higher commit band). For large-volume customers we will map these bands into a discount ladder: at 1.25x realized usage we apply a 3% effective discount to the base rate; at 1.5x realized usage we apply 5% effective discount (applied retroactively on the tier). This avoids double-charging while incentivizing broader adoption.

5) Early exit credits
- Standard: unused prepaid commit may be credited on termination on a declining schedule (year 1: 80% refundable, year 2: 50%, year 3+: non-refundable), subject to minimum contract runout and audit-confirmed usage. We can negotiate carve-outs for pilots and proof-of-value pilots.

Worked example summary (high-level) — attached as a pricing grid: three-year commit $1.2M USD/year (annual true-up):
- Indexation option: CPI cap +3% applied each anniversary (floor 0%).
- Overage ladder: 0–10% at 1.25x, 10–35% at 1.15x, >35% at 1.0x (converts to next commit band; discount ladder applies retroactively).
- True-up cadence: quarterly invoice with annual aggregation for accounting.

Attachments: RLX-commit-pricing-grid-v1.xlsx (pricing grid and worked numbers), Appendix-Price-Indexation.pdf (clause examples).

Next steps: propose a 30-minute call Thu/ Fri to review the worked example and confirm which indexation option you prefer.

John —

Appreciate the follow-up. Per internal alignment, we’ve finalized a recommended commercial template that balances predictability and scale incentives. Summary below and attached are the worked numbers from the grid.

Key commercial points (final):
- Indexation: option to index to US CPI-U annually; standard cap +3.0% and floor 0%. For multiyear commitments of 3+ years we can increase cap to +4.0% by mutual consent (documented in SOW).
- FX: invoice currency selectable per region; fixed-USD invoicing available with 0.5% admin fee and quarterly reconciliation.
- Commit smoothing: rolling quarterly smoothing window with 15% per-quarter grace band. Quarterly true-ups, 12-month carry-forward for under-usage.
- Overage tiers: marginal bands — 0–10% at 1.25x, 10–35% at 1.15x, >35% at 1.0x (converts to higher commit band); retroactive volume discounts: 3% effective @1.25x, 5% effective @1.5x. Promotional 7% @1.75x reserved for strategic reference customers and requires signoff from VP Sales.
- Early exit: unused prepaid commit credit schedule (year 1: 80%, year 2: 50%, year 3+: 0%), subject to audit.

Attached: RLX-commit-pricing-grid-v1.xlsx (worked three-year model) and Appendix-Price-Indexation.pdf (sample contract language). I’ve also generated a short PDF summary if you want a one-pager for procurement.

If the above aligns, next steps are: 1) confirm indexation option (A or B), 2) select desired commit term (24 vs 36 months) and 3) we’ll issue a non-binding commercial term sheet and schedule a legal review call.
